item.text: {"text":"Closest prior work: Aleksandr Petrov and Craig Macdonald, [“Effective and Efficient Training for Sequential Recommendation using Recency Sampling” (RecSys 2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643), subsequently extended as RSS. Their [original implementation](https://github.com/asash/bert4rec_repro) includes `RecencySequenceSampling`: draw c=max(1,floor(nτ)) positions with replacement, then deduplicate. Default exponential weights give per-draw p(k)=(1−α)α^(n−1−k)/(1−α^n), α=0.8; endpoint probability is 0.2/(1−0.8^n), approaching 0.2. Its probability of inclusion among c draws is 1−(1−p(k))^c. No separate endpoint branch. RSS removes selected items and predicts them jointly from the remaining sequence, which can retain interactions after a target; it is not prefix-only masked-item prediction. [Sampler code](https://github.com/asash/bert4rec_repro/blob/main/recommenders/dnn_sequential_recommender/targetsplitters/recency_sequence_sampling.py).\n\nFor the proposed single-target policy, let m be the number of eligible nonterminal positions and r=min(10,m). Assuming m>0, P(endpoint)=0.1 and P(k)=0.45/m+0.45·1[k in latest r]/r. This produces a uniform floor plus a recent-window step, unlike RSS’s geometric decay; for short histories, nonterminal probabilities can exceed the endpoint’s. Prefix truncation would be a substantive objective difference, but the stated sampling probabilities alone do not establish it. RSS samples before retaining the latest maximum-length remaining history ([vectorizer](https://github.com/asash/bert4rec_repro/blob/main/recommenders/dnn_sequential_recommender/history_vectorizers/default_history_vectorizer.py)). Its [BCE implementation](https://github.com/asash/bert4rec_repro/blob/main/losses/bce.py) divides summed loss by all eligible item-label entries, not sampled-positive count; the paper also evaluates LambdaRank. The proposed policy specifies no loss normalization. Assessment: a distinct sampling distribution, but recency-biased target selection is established prior work; stronger differentiation depends on context construction and objective, with controlled validation needed."}
